A former Minister of State for Niger Delta Affairs and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Senator Tayo Alasoadura, has said the party has achieved over 70 per cent of its nationwide mobilisation and coordination efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections. Alasoadura expressed confidence that the APC would secure victory for President Bola Tinubu if party leaders and stakeholders sustained their commitment to the mobilisation exercise. In a statement personally signed by him on Monday, the former minister described nationwide political mobilisation as an extensive and demanding task but said the party had made considerable progress. According to him, the party had achieved well over 70 per cent of the required coordination nationwide. “The task of organising and sustaining a nationwide political mobilisation structure is extensive and demanding. Considerable progress has already been made.The APC has achieved well over 70 per cent of its required coordination nationwide. Maintaining the current momentum would translate into electoral success,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Tinubu asked me to sustain South-West security operations, says Igboho Ondo community protests alleged planned imposition of monarch 2027: INEC selects 17,676 polling units for BVAS mock exercise Speaking on regional mobilisation, Alasoadura said political leaders across the South-West were working to consolidate support for Tinubu, particularly to ensure a decisive victory for the President in Ondo State. He stressed the need for unity, effective coordination and sustained engagement among party members, noting that the success of the mobilisation exercise depended on the collective commitment of leaders and members at all levels. He expressed optimism that the party’s ongoing efforts would translate into electoral success in the 2027 general elections. He commended the APC National Chairman, members of the National Working Committee, the leadership of the Presidential Campaign Council and other party stakeholders for their efforts in coordinating the party’s activities. The APC is intensifying efforts to strengthen its nationwide political structures and mobilise support for the 2027 general elections, in which President Bola Tinubu is expected to seek re-election. The party has continued to engage its leaders and stakeholders across the six geopolitical zones to consolidate its support base, with the South-West, Tinubu’s home region, expected to play a significant role in its re-election bid.
